label: April 20–26
title: “All That the Lord Hath Spoken We Will Do” —  Exodus 19–20; 24; 31

items.text: When Moses read the law, the children of Israel covenanted, “All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient.” This promise was made despite past murmurings and wavering. It shows their willingness to commit to God’s word, even when faced with challenges.

God desired a tabernacle so “that I may dwell among them.” This reveals His deep longing to be present with His people. Even when we falter, His desire to dwell among us remains a constant, encouraging truth.

Faith and commitment can be overcome by impatience, fear, or doubt. The Israelites turned to an idol soon after promising to “have no other gods.” Yet, the Lord is merciful and does not give up on us, for He is abundant in goodness and truth.

President Russell M. Nelson taught that the Hebrew term translated as “peculiar” means ‘valued property,’ or ‘treasure.’ To be called God's peculiar people is a compliment of the highest order, signifying that we are precious and highly valued by Him.

Sacred experiences require preparation. The Lord instructed the children of Israel to be prepared before they could “meet with God.” This principle applies to us today; we must prepare ourselves spiritually for sacred ordinances like the sacrament and temple covenants.

Obedience to God’s commandments brings blessings. The Ten Commandments, given at Mount Sinai, are not exhaustive but emphasize crucial principles. Keeping these commandments helps us live the two great commandments of loving God and loving our neighbor.

Putting God first yields significant blessings. When we are tempted to place other things before Him, remembering the blessings that come from prioritizing God helps us maintain our focus. The hymn “How Gentle God’s Commands” can guide us in this.

Making covenants with God demonstrates our sincere willingness to obey His law. While ancient covenants had rituals different from today, the principle of covenant making remains. These sacred agreements are pathways to drawing closer to Him.

Sin is the act of turning away from God. Repentance, however, is the powerful process of turning toward Him and deliberately turning away from evil. This turning is essential for spiritual healing and returning to His embrace.

The Lord’s enduring love for His covenant people is a profound truth. Despite Israel’s lapses, God’s promise of mercy and His desire to dwell among them never wavered. He extends this same patience and love to us today.
